questions.stem: In physics, what does 'Escape Velocity' refer to?

options.option_text: The minimum speed an object needs to break free from a planet's gravitational pull without further propulsion
The speed at which an airplane breaks the sound barrier
The maximum speed an object can reach while falling through the atmosphere
The speed required to establish a stable circular orbit around a planet

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Escape velocity is the minimum speed needed for a free, non-propelled object to escape from the gravitational influence of a massive body (like Earth) completely. For Earth, the escape velocity at the surface is about 11.2 km/s (or roughly 25,000 mph).
DECOY BUSTING: Breaking the sound barrier is Mach 1. The maximum falling speed is 'Terminal Velocity'. The speed to maintain an orbit is 'Orbital Velocity' (which is lower than escape velocity).
EXAM INSIGHT: Escape velocity depends entirely on the mass and radius of the planet. It does NOT depend on the mass of the escaping object (a feather and a rocket need the same escape velocity).
